narrative.overview:
Whiffle is a board an operator glances at between other work. It answers one question: does anything need me right now? The design treats that glance like reading a departure board. Rows hold still, numbers line up, and a quiet row has to mean a healthy row. The name comes from the code. The status dots are "the Quiet Ledger status hues" (`ActivityDot.svelte`), the slash menu "wears Quiet Ledger tokens" (`Composer.svelte`), and the copy guide calls the voice "a calm ledger, not a personality brand" (`WORDS.md`).

The surface is graphite ink on cool, near-neutral paper. Chroma is close to zero in all chrome; the neutral ramp carries a faint blue cast (hue around 260) that reads as cool rather than grey. Colour is spent on four things only: status, identity marks, the blue focus ring, and data that crosses a threshold. The primary action is graphite with a soft top highlight, never a hue. Depth comes from a recessed frame holding raised content, not from heavy shadows. The density is set by the operator's job: 44px rows, a 32px header band, 90px stat tiles and the 14px body size. Pages are efficient without being cramped.

Motion is continuity, never decoration. Something that exists on both sides of a change travels to its new place rather than vanishing and reappearing, and a list that changes reflows rather than jumps. Nothing moves after it has landed unless it is live work, and live work breathes slowly. The visual rejection is explicit in the code: no ease-in curve, no `rgba(0,0,0,…)` shadow, no weight above 500, no indigo, no hue used for decoration.
keyCharacteristics: Graphite action, cool paper surfaces, colour only where it carries meaning.
The frame recesses; content sits raised on it.
Two type families: Geist for everything, TX-02 for code, paths and IDs. Weights 400 and 500 only.
A spacing ladder measured off the reference comps (4, 7, 11, 14, 18, 21, 25, 32), not a 4px grid.
Solar bold-duotone icons throughout, linear only for chevrons and arrows.
Motion that keeps one object on screen through every change, honours reduced motion everywhere, and exits faster than it enters.

rules.name: The No Ease-In Rule
rules.body: No ease-in curve exists. Anything that starts slow feels like the interface hesitating.

rules.name: The Fast Exit Rule
rules.body: Exits are shorter than entrances. A popover opens over 260ms and closes over 160ms. A dialog opens over 280ms and closes over 160ms. A toast rises over 280ms and leaves over 160ms.

rules.name: The One Object Rule
rules.body: What is on both sides of a change travels; it never vanishes on one side and appears on the other (`motion/share.svelte.ts`). A sidebar row becomes the tab it opens, a section row's title flies into the editor header, a sent message flies from the composer into the transcript row it became. A flight runs 280ms on the drawer curve, as a transform (FLIP) or a clip that opens from the source's box. The source is hidden while its copy flies, so the screen never shows two.

rules.name: The Nothing Jumps Rule
rules.body: When a list changes, rows that stay slide to their new places, rows that leave close while fading, and rows that arrive are uncovered top to bottom while what follows makes room (`motion/rows.svelte.ts`). Movement takes 280ms on ease-in-out, arrivals fade over 260ms, departures fade over 160ms, all started on the same frame. A move that happens entirely off screen jumps instead of sliding, so nothing drifts into view behind the reader's scroll.

rules.name: The Interruptible Rule
rules.body: Every transition turns back from where it is drawn. Popovers transition on `data-state` rather than playing keyframes, folds animate from the drawn height, and a segmented thumb caught mid-glide restarts from where it stands.

rules.name: The One Loop Rule
rules.body: Anything that turns or blinks while something is pending runs one ambient loop, `--dur-loop` (1.2s): a spinner, the task ring's arc, the supervisor's orbit, the skeleton's sweep, and Tailwind's `animate-spin`, `animate-pulse` and `animate-ping`, which the theme points at the token. A rotation turns linearly; a pulse runs ease-in-out and a ping ease-out. Longer rhythms are multiples of the breath, never new numbers: the thinking indicator's words change every two breaths. Tailwind's default transition timing (`transition-colors` and its siblings) is `--dur-control` on ease-out.

rules.name: The Reduced Motion Rule
rules.body: Motion is opt-in. Every travelling transition and keyframe sits under `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference`, and JavaScript motion asks the same question through `motionOk` (`motion/curves.svelte.ts`). With reduced motion, opacity and colour fades still run, pages cross-fade in place over 120ms, heights land at once, folds fade instead of opening, list changes only fade, flights do not fly, and loops stop (an indeterminate spinner keeps turning). Reduced motion means stillness. It does not mean an instant swap.

rules.name: The Dark Flips Polarity Rule
rules.body: At night a groove sits below the card (recess-deep is neutral-1) and a lifted thumb sits above it (neutral-6). Dark mode is a second set of lightness decisions, never an inverted light mode.

rules.name: The Reserved Hue Rule
rules.body: Red, amber, green and blue mean status, and status only. Progress rings, identity and decoration take `currentColor` or an identity hue. A finished task ring is the one moment a decoration earns a state colour, because by then it is a result (`TaskRing.svelte`).

rules.name: The Graphite Action Rule
rules.body: The action is graphite, never a hue. A hue-filled primary button does not exist in this system.

rules.name: The Blue Is Focus Rule
rules.body: The blue accent marks where the keyboard is and what is selected. It never fills a button, a chip or a background.

rules.name: The Idle Has No Fill Rule
rules.body: An idle session carries no chip. A quiet row means a healthy row, so rest is drawn as nothing.

rules.name: The No Indigo Rule
rules.body: Indigo is never a brand, action or accent hue. The accent is a blue at hue 263 and is reserved for focus. Identity hues span the wheel for telling things apart and are never promoted to a brand role.

rules.name: The Glyph, Word, Hue Rule
rules.body: Status is never colour alone. The session status reads glyph, then word, then hue (a Solar duotone glyph, then "Working", "Needs you", "Failed", "Idle", "Sleeping", "Stopped" or "Unreachable"). The activity dot changes shape as well as colour: Needs you pings, Unreachable is hollow, Sleeping is a moon. A board chip carries the word inside its tint.

rules.name: The 500 Ceiling Rule
rules.body: No weight above 500 exists. Emphasis is a weight step from 400 to 500 or an ink step, never bold. The prose plugin's 600 to 800 weights are overridden back to 500.

rules.name: The Role, Not Size Rule
rules.body: Text takes a role by what it does. Names, group headings, column heads and badges are label. Sentences and descriptions are body. Timestamps, counts, units and hints are meta. Nobody picks a size and finds a role for it.

rules.name: The Tabular Figure Rule
rules.body: A figure that changes (a count, a price, an age, a percentage) carries `.num` and is set in tabular numerals, so a ticking value never moves its neighbours. Tables get tabular numerals by default. The KPI role always carries `.num`, because a `font` shorthand resets `font-variant-numeric`.

rules.name: The Truncate Inside Rule
rules.body: Text truncates with an ellipsis in an inner span, never on the control or link itself, so the hit area is never clipped. In a row, the name gives way first and the meta line keeps one line.

rules.name: The 16px Field Rule
rules.body: On a phone or a coarse pointer every text field renders at 16px (an `!important` in the base layer), because iOS Safari zooms into any field under 16px.

rules.name: The Frame Recesses Rule
rules.body: The frame recesses and content never does. The one sanctioned card-in-card is the stat tile's recessed well, which the reference plan calls "a signature move of the design".

rules.name: The Graphite Shadow Rule
rules.body: Shadows are cool graphite taken from the neutral ramp, never `rgba(0,0,0,·)`.

rules.name: The Dark Changes Shape Rule
rules.body: At night elevation changes shape as well as colour. A raised thumb is an inset hairline and the ladder aliases the doctrine set, keyed on the theme class rather than `light-dark()`.

rules.name: The Concentric Rule
rules.body: A surface nested inside another takes the outer radius less the inset. The dialog tray (18px, 6px padding) holds a 12px body. The composer shell (12px, 7px inset) holds 5px controls, and the autopilot's halo 3px outside its control is drawn at 8px. A subagent's well (8px, 4px padding) holds a 5px report.

rules.name: The Measured Exception Rule
rules.body: The stat tile keeps the comp's measured radii (a 10px card around a 7px well, 7px in), even though a concentric well would be 3px.

rules.name: The Press Rule
rules.body: The hand feels a control before release, in one of two ways chosen by size. A compact standalone control (a button, an icon button, a chip, a switch, about 44px tall at most) scales to 0.97 over 160ms on ease-out. Anything wide, large or grouped (rows, cards, card heads, tabs in a strip, segments) tints to `surface-fill` and moves nothing, because a 0.97 scale pulls a 300px row's edge in by 4.5px. A text link dims to 72% opacity. The scale only runs with motion allowed; the tint always runs.

rules.name: The Hold-To-Select Rule
rules.body: A press that starts inside a text field in a drawer is not captured by the drawer, so iOS hold-to-select and the Paste callout still reach the field. A held press on a context-menu trigger suppresses the platform callout, because our menu answers it.

rules.name: The Claim Of Nothing Rule
rules.body: An empty state claims there is nothing to show, so it renders only once the data is known to be empty, never while it is still being read. While data loads, the skeleton stands in at the real layout's size, and the first real read replaces it in one cross-fade (120ms) rather than as rows arriving.

rules.name: The Composer Touch Rule
rules.body: The textarea sits above its label's touch area, so a press on the text lands on the field itself and iOS hold-to-select and Paste reach it.

rules.name: The Peer Rule
rules.body: Approve and Deny are recessed peers: the same secondary fill and hairline edge, the same 32px height (44px on a coarse pointer), the same label type. They differ in kind, never in salience: Approve carries a tick in `ink-strong` and Deny a cross in `ink-muted`. Both clear AA on the recess fill (ink-strong 12.39:1 and ink-muted 5.47:1 by day, 13.92:1 and 8.50:1 at night). They stand at opposite ends of the row with at least 32px between them, and no third control may sit in that gap.

rules.name: The Consequential Grant Rule
rules.body: A standing grant ("Always allow … for …") is a wider grant than the request, so it is kept apart: under a 32px break and a hairline, after a sentence saying what it would allow, and drawn in the warning tint with warning ink, a shield glyph and a real edge. It is the most salient control on the card on purpose. The raw tool input sits behind a "What this touches" disclosure, so a grant can be informed.

rules.name: The Solar Duotone Rule
rules.body: Every product icon is Solar's bold-duotone cut, imported through `$lib/icons.ts`: one face for the whole product. The duotone's second layer is the same `currentColor` at 50% opacity. Chevrons and arrows (`alt-arrow-*`, `arrow-*`) use Solar's linear cut because they are glyphs, not marks. Close, Minus, Plus and Tick are local glyphs drawn to Solar's 24px grid with a 1.5 linear stroke and round caps, because Solar has no bare version.

rules.name: The One Ring Rule
rules.body: Every focusable element shows one ring on keyboard focus only: a 2px solid outline in `focus-ring`, 2px outside the element. Text fields, list rows, tabs, options and anything flush against a container or inside a clipping scroller carry the ring inset on their own border box instead, so it never stacks on a border or gets cut. The ring's colour is set at rest, so focus only switches it on. A scroller brings a focused control into view with room for its ring. Pointer focus shows nothing.

rules.name: The 44 Touch Rule
rules.body: On a coarse pointer every control's tappable area reaches 44×44 through a transparent `::after` (`.touch-hit`, WCAG 2.5.8), while its drawn size and the layout stay the same. Where neighbours sit closer, `--hit-gap-x` and `--hit-gap-y` stop each area at the midpoint so areas never overlap; clusters open their gap on touch (8 to 14px for a row's controls, to 16px in the top bar). A scroller that would clip the areas pads into an equal negative margin. Menu items and nav rows are 44px tall on touch.

rules.name: The 24 Pointer Rule
rules.body: On a fine pointer, a control drawn smaller than 24×24 reaches 24px through `.pointer-hit`, with the same midpoint stops. `--hit-scale` keeps the area at 24px on screen inside a zoomed canvas.

dos: **Do** take every colour, radius, type role, spacing step, curve and duration from the tokens in `app.css`. Add a token before adding a one-off value.
**Do** keep the action graphite with its top-highlight gradient, and spend hue only on status, identity, focus and threshold data.
**Do** recess the frame and raise the content; the stat well is the only card-in-card.
**Do** say status with a glyph or a word before hue, and draw idle as no chip at all.
**Do** set every changing figure in tabular numerals (`.num`), and keep weights at 400 and 500.
**Do** use Solar bold-duotone for every product icon, linear only for chevrons and arrows, at 12, 16 or 20px.
**Do** make a compact control scale to 0.97 on press and a wide or grouped one tint to `surface-fill`.
**Do** give every touch control a 44×44 area and every small pointer target a 24×24 area without changing the drawn size.
**Do** enter on ease-out over 260 to 280ms and leave over 160ms; move things already on screen on ease-in-out.
**Do** carry shared objects across a change, and reflow lists rather than letting rows jump.
**Do** put every travelling motion under `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference` (or `motionOk` in script), and keep fades for reduced motion.
**Do** show a skeleton at the real layout's size while data loads, and the empty state only once the data is known to be empty.
**Do** keep Approve and Deny as equal peers at opposite ends of their row, with the standing grant set apart below.
donts: **Don't** fill an action, chip or background with the blue accent, or introduce indigo anywhere as a brand or accent hue.
**Don't** use a hue for decoration, or use red, amber, green or blue for anything but status.
**Don't** set any text above weight 500, or pick a size without a role.
**Don't** use `rgba(0,0,0,·)` shadows; shadows come from the graphite tints.
**Don't** use an ease-in curve, or let an exit run longer than its entrance.
**Don't** keep an arrived surface moving: no pulse or attention loop on anything that is not live work.
**Don't** draw a focus indicator as a box-shadow, a border-colour change or a background, and don't stack a ring on a border.
**Don't** truncate on the control or link itself, which clips its hit area.
**Don't** render a text field under 16px on a phone or a coarse pointer.
**Don't** swap Solar for another icon set or for SF Symbols, or drop the duotone layer.
**Don't** use pill-shaped buttons; full rounding is for state pills, switches and dots.
**Don't** put a third control between Approve and Deny, or make one more salient than the other.
**Don't** show an empty state while data is loading, or claim zero while the hub connection is not live.
